answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This holds because each vote is weighted by a track record that only grows through honest participation, turning a Sybil flood into short-lived, low-weight votes. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a nectar as the anchor of the cost.
